An orchestration must have two or three foundation or processing dependencies and must not mix them.

What the Standard says

“Dependency Balance (Florance Pattern)” — An orchestration combines foundation or processing services to complete a business flow while keeping its dependencies balanced at one architectural level. read it here.
“Two-Three” — The two-three rule limits an orchestration to two or three dependencies, keeping the flow focused and preventing it from becoming an uncontrolled coordination layer. read it here.

Why it matters

An orchestration combines two or three foundation or processing capabilities into one business flow. Mixing dependency levels obscures the abstraction boundary, while too many collaborators make the workflow difficult to protect, test, and reason about.

Bad code example

// Violates STXO001: An orchestration must have two or three foundation or processing dependencies and must not mix them.
class StudentOrchestrationService(
    IStudentService students,
    ISchoolProcessingService schools) : IStudentOrchestrationService { }

Good code example

// Follows STXO001
class StudentOrchestrationService(
    IStudentService students,
    ISchoolService schools) : IStudentOrchestrationService { }
